free_tier.stated: The Activate Founders tier offers USD 1,000 in AWS Activate Credits, plus USD 350 in AWS Developer Support credits, valid for two years. Eligibility: new to AWS Activate Credits, self-funded, a fully functioning company website, founded in the past 10 years, and a business email matching the startup domain. AWS states: 'If you do not have an Org ID, you are initially eligible for the Founders Package.'

egress.terms: not published: the page read states no egress allowance and no overage price; the credits guide says standard AWS rates apply when credits run out; read 2026-11-03

interface_detail: console only for the credit grant: a web application with an AWS Builder ID, credits viewed in the AWS console under Billing; the guide documents no API for the grant

chaining: USD 1,000 of EC2 and S3 plus USD 350 of Developer Support is the cheapest entry point at AWS and it does not disqualify a later Portfolio application, so the chain is Founders now, Portfolio after any accelerator affiliation. It composes with the Kiro Startup Credits promotion, which excludes applicants who already hold Activate credits.

limits.value: The review fails first: AWS has unpublished internal requirements, applications go unedited once submitted, and reports of repeated rejection for legitimate applicants are common. After approval the two-year expiry and the USD 1,000 size are what bind.

identity_cost.detail: No incorporation requirement appears in the English eligibility list or the seven-step application guide. The gates are an AWS Builder ID, a business email matching a startup domain (the guide says to use the business email for the Builder ID and the Activate profile), a live company website, and a linked AWS account. This corrected an earlier version of this finding, which recorded fails-identity on the assumption that a company was required.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed in this session

evidence.proved: the Founders eligibility list is new to Activate, self-funded, a fully functioning company website and founded in the past 10 years, with no incorporation term, quoted
'If you do not have an Org ID, you are initially eligible for the Founders Package', and the guide requires a business email matching the startup domain, quoted

the Japanese AWS page lists the required fields for Founders as an AWS account ID, a company website or web profile, and the applicant's LinkedIn profile, and states crowdfunding and friends-and-family funded startups remain eligible, quoted and translated
an AWS re:Post answer states that meeting the published criteria does not guarantee approval and that AWS has internal requirements beyond the public list, reported
after credits end, AWS standard rates apply; the guide states no egress allowance or price
evidence.quote: You'll be charged the standard rates for any ongoing AWS services when your credits run out or if the expiration date passes.

evidence.proved: credits are applied to an AWS account and viewed in the console
evidence.quote: You can view your credits balance and expiration date in your AWS Console under Billing --> Credits.

notes: A first pass recorded this as fails-identity on the assumption that a company was required; the evidence reversed that verdict in the same session. AWS's seven-step application guide and its Japanese getting-started page both name a website, a domain business email and a LinkedIn profile rather than a legal entity, and one third-party tracker records solo-founder eligibility as yes. The residual risk is the unpublished internal review, which is where rejections actually happen. The corpus record dossier/storage/aws-activate.json merges both tiers and marks it qualifies-with-caveat with a garbled derived identity_cost; its numbers stand, its identity field does not.
